parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.stem: Bleach is used as a cleaning product to kill bacteria. It is made by adding compounds like sodium chlorate(I), $\text{NaClO}$, to water.
parts.text: Identify the formula of the ion present in bleach that kills bacteria.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text:
Sodium chlorate(I), $\text{NaClO}$, reacts with hydrogen peroxide to produce sodium chloride, water and oxygen gas.

Construct an equation for this reaction.

parts.label: (e)(iii)
parts.text:
A sample of bleach $\mathbf{W}$ contains an unknown concentration of sodium chlorate(I).

$10.0\text{ cm}^3$ of $\mathbf{W}$ is diluted with distilled water to make a total volume of $100\text{ cm}^3$ of bleach solution. $25.0\text{ cm}^3$ of this diluted bleach solution is added to an excess of hydrogen peroxide and the volume of gas produced measured under room conditions. The experiment is repeated and on average $25.0\text{ cm}^3$ of diluted bleach solution produces $42.0\text{ cm}^3$ of gas.

Calculate the concentration, in $\text{g dm}^{-3}$, of sodium chlorate(I) in $\mathbf{W}$.
